english.html: ble to judge or condemn that man. And so in civil matters: for a wicked man could easily cause a rumour of false things to be sown, to serve his cause. Wherefore our laws have holily ordained that proof by rumour and common repute is not full proof <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, save in certain cases collected by our interpreters in the common places <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>: as when it is a question of proving the bounds and limits of lands <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>; or of showing certain old and ancient facts exceeding the memory of men <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>; or else of making it appear that Jean is the son of Antoine, Pierre the son of François, or any other filiation <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>; or of proving the death of someone <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>; or of putting in evidence some other thing which cannot be proved save with great difficulty. And although in civil matters it is received that rumour and renown make a half-proof, nevertheless in criminal causes (of which we are speaking), or indeed in civil ones that are high and grave, this has no place <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. Wherefore the judge could not then join this half-proof with one witness, to make it full and entire <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>.

Testium fides), § Eiusdem (D. 22.5.3.2, Hadrian's rescript: witnesses are weighed, and consentiens fama may confirm belief in a fact); the Gloss on Decretals X 5.27 (De clerico excommunicato, deposito vel interdicto ministrante), c. Illud (chapter number unverified)
notes.original: l. iij P eiuſ dé D de teſti. Gloſe au c. illud. de cleri. excom.
notes.gloss: The P. is the print's sort for §; eiuſ dé is eiuſdẽ (eiusdem) with a reflow gap and a wrong sort.

notes.citation: Felinus Sandeus (Felin) on Decretals X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Veniens, the first of the two chapters so beginning in that title (chapter number unverified)
notes.original: Felin au c. veniens. i de teſti.
notes.gloss: Felinus's commentary collects the cases in which fama is admitted as proof; the same place is cited at annot-041 {a}.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Cum causam (chapter number unverified)
notes.gloss: The boundaries of lands may be proved by repute; cited at annot-028 {c2} as well.

notes.citation: Innocent IV on the said Decretals X 2.20, c. Veniens
notes.gloss: Aud. = au d[it], "at the said chapter". Innocent's commentary admits common repute for facts beyond living memory.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.19 (De probationibus), c. Per tuas (chapter number unverified)
notes.gloss: Filiation proved by common repute; as at annot-041 {b}.

notes.citation: Bartolus (Bartole) on Digest 29.3 (Testamenta quemadmodum aperiantur, inspiciantur et describantur), l. 3 as printed, § Si dubitetur (cf. D. 29.3.2, Ulpian, where that paragraph stands; the law number differs from annot-041 {o}, which gives l. ij)
notes.original: Bartole en la l. iij. P. ſi du bitetur. D quẽ admod. teſta. aper.
notes.gloss: Bartolus there admits proof of a testator's death by common repute; du bitetur is dubitetur with a reflow gap.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Tam litteris and c. Veniens (chapter numbers unverified)
notes.original: c. tam lite. ris. c. veniens; de teſti.
notes.gloss: Lite. ris is literis broken by a reflow gap with a stray point; the semicolon after veniens is a stray sort for a point. The same pair is cited together at texte-57's Annotation LX, note p.

notes.citation: The said c. Tam litteris (X 2.20); Felinus Sandeus (Felin) on the said c. Veniens (X 2.20)
notes.original: c. tam literis. alleguee; Felin. aud. c; veniens.
notes.gloss: Alleguee = "already cited"; aud. c. = au dit chapitre. Reading B c. is taken over the print's c;, the semicolon being a stray sort in the abbreviation c. (capitulum).

notes.citation: Accursius (Accurse), the Gloss on Digest 22.5.3 (De testibus, l. 3), § Eiusdem (D. 22.5.3.2); Salicetus (Salicet; Bartholomaeus de Saliceto) on Code 9.2 (De accusationibus et inscriptionibus), l. Ea quidem, at the last paragraph, towards its end (the law not numbered; unverified)
notes.original: Accurſe en la l. iij P. eiuſdé. D. de teſt. Salicet en la l. ea quidẽ. P. fin ſur la fin. C. de accuſa.
notes.gloss: The Gloss on § Eiusdem is where the doctrine of fama as half-proof is built; P. fin ſur la fin = § fin., in fine. Reading A quidẽ (= quidem) is taken over quidé.

readings.reason: quidẽ = quidem, the incipit l. Ea quidem (C. de accusationibus); quidé with an acute is not a Latin word.
c. is the standard abbreviation for capitulum before veniens; the semicolon in c; is a stray sort for the point.
